name: Provedly – Verified Sales Popup & Social Proof for WooCommerce
author: elminson

sections.description:
Provedly adds a sales popup to your WooCommerce store: recent sales notifications like “Maria L. just purchased Linen Shirt”, a live visitor counter, a real order count and countdown timer bars. It is social proof and FOMO built only from real data, so every notification is something your shoppers can check.

Features

  • Recent sales notifications from your WooCommerce orders, with the buyer’s first name and last initial (you choose the name format), city, product and time.
  • Verified purchase mark on every order that reached Provedly over a webhook signed with your secret.
  • Live visitor counter: a real count of visitors on the page in the last 90 seconds. No setting can raise it.
  • Real orders bar: how many verified orders your store took in the last 24 hours, 7 days or 30 days, hidden below a minimum you set.
  • Countdown timer and announcement bars: countdowns to a date, evergreen timers and plain announcement bars with a button.
  • Verification page: every badge links to a public page your shoppers can check.
  • Attribution: see which orders followed a notification the buyer saw.
  • Lightweight: one small async script, rendered in a Shadow DOM so it does not clash with your theme.
  • Preview before connecting: the plugin page shows an example notification and bar, and how many of your recent orders could appear.

Why verified, not fake FOMO

Many sales popup plugins invent buyers, loop the same orders or show a visitor count that is just a random number. Shoppers notice, and it costs you trust. Provedly only shows what really happened:

  • Orders arrive from WooCommerce over a webhook signed with your secret, and only those get the “Verified purchase” mark.
  • The live counter cannot be set or inflated.
  • Countdown bars end when they say they end. Evergreen timers are disclosed as per-visitor on the public verification page.

One-click connect

Connecting takes one click: no tokens or code to copy. This plugin then does three things: loads your Provedly notifications and bars on every page through one small site loader script, creates the WooCommerce webhooks that deliver orders to Provedly (one for new orders, one for status changes), and passes the widget’s anonymous visitor id to the order so Provedly can tell you which orders followed a notification.

The notification widget and the bars work on any WordPress site. Verified purchases need WooCommerce.

Free plan

A free Provedly account at https://provedly.app includes 2,000 impressions a month, with verified purchases included. Paid plans add more impressions.

This plugin is free software under the GPLv2 or later, like every plugin in this directory: you can read, change and share its code. Provedly itself (the dashboard, the verification pages and the notification service) is a hosted service with its own terms and is not part of this plugin.

External services

This plugin connects to Provedly (https://provedly.app), a hosted social-proof service, only after you click “Connect to Provedly” or enter a widget token or webhook URL on its settings page. It makes no network requests before that.

What is sent and when:

  • When you click “Connect to Provedly”, your browser goes to provedly.app with your site address, your site name, whether WooCommerce is active and a one-time security code. After you confirm, WordPress sends the one-time code and your site address to provedly.app once, to receive your site key, the WooCommerce webhook URL and its signing secret.
  • Storefront pages load the widget and bar scripts from provedly.app and send them anonymous usage events (page path, a random visitor id stored in the shopper’s browser, and the notification shown or clicked). Provedly stores only a hash of the visitor id.
  • When an order is placed or its status changes, WooCommerce delivers the order to your Provedly webhook URL over HTTPS, signed with the secret you chose: customer name, city, state, country, line items, total, currency, order id and the visitor id from the order meta. Card numbers and full street addresses are never sent.

Provedly terms of service: https://provedly.app/terms
Provedly privacy policy: https://provedly.app/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin. The Provedly page opens with a preview of what shoppers will see.
  2. Click “Connect to Provedly”.
  3. Sign in or create a free Provedly account and confirm this site.
  4. You’re back in WordPress, connected: notifications and bars load on your store, and the WooCommerce webhooks and their secret are set up for you, so orders arrive as Verified purchases.

Place a test order to check it: it appears in Provedly within seconds with the verified mark.

Prefer to paste tokens yourself? Open “Manual setup (advanced)” on the Provedly page.
sections.faq:
Is this a fake sales popup?

No. Notifications come from real orders, and only orders delivered over your signed WooCommerce webhook show the “Verified purchase” mark. Records you add by hand or import are labelled as such. The preview on the plugin page is marked as an example and is never shown on your store.

Is there a free plan?

Yes. The free plan includes 2,000 impressions a month, with verified purchases included. No card is needed to start.

Does it work in my language?

The plugin’s admin page is translated into Spanish, Portuguese (Brazil), French and German, and you can add more on translate.wordpress.org.

How do I disconnect?

Open Provedly in the admin menu and click Disconnect. The plugin stops loading Provedly on your store and removes the WooCommerce webhooks it created. Deleting the plugin does the same and removes its settings.

Does the plugin slow my store down?

It prints one script tag (the site loader). The widget bundle is about 6 KB gzipped, loads async and renders in a Shadow DOM.

What data is sent to Provedly?

Order webhooks as WooCommerce sends them (customer name, city, country, items, total) and the widget’s anonymous visitor id. Provedly stores a hash of the visitor id. See https://provedly.app/privacy.

Do I need WooCommerce?

The widget and bars work on any WordPress site. Order sync needs WooCommerce 7 or newer.
sections.changelog:
1.1.2

  • Preview before connecting: an example sales notification and bar, clearly labelled, and how many of your paid WooCommerce orders from the last 30 days can appear as Verified purchases.
  • Translations: Spanish, Portuguese (Brazil), French and German bundled, plus a .pot file for other languages.
  • Clearer plugin name and description.

1.1.1

  • Redesigned settings page: clear connect flow, health checks, version shown in the header.
  • Cash on delivery, bank transfer and cheque orders now reach Provedly at checkout: the plugin adds an order.created webhook next to order.updated (existing sites get it automatically after the update).
  • Docs and Support links on the Plugins screen.

1.1.0

  • One-click Connect to Provedly: no tokens to copy.
  • Loads everything through the site loader.
  • WooCommerce webhook and secret set up automatically.
  • Uninstall cleans up the webhook.

1.0.3

  • Provedly now has its own admin menu item with the Provedly icon, and the settings page shows the logo and a link to your dashboard. The old Settings, Provedly address redirects there.

1.0.2

  • Fix: read the widget’s visitor cookie so orders are attributed to the notifications the buyer saw.

1.0.1

  • Readme: clearer description, real orders bar.

1.0.0

  • First release: storefront scripts, webhook setup, visitor attribution.
